html:
La Sape is the culture of the sapeurs, men of Brazzaville and Kinshasa who dress in expensive designer suits and parade their elegance in the streets.

The name stands for a French phrase meaning the society of ambiance makers and elegant people. Its roots lie in colonial times, when African clerks and servants in Brazzaville took up European dress with flair. It grew in the 1960s and 1970s in the Bacongo quarter and was spread in Kinshasa by the singer Papa Wemba and other stars of Congolese rumba.

Sapeurs can spend far beyond their means on clothes, and the movement has been read as joy, protest and a claim to dignity in hard times. Photographs of sapeurs made it famous around the world.
sum: La Sape is the culture of the sapeurs, men of Brazzaville and Kinshasa who dress in expensive designer suits and parade their elegance in the streets.
